steps.intent: Our primary objectives are to reinforce the advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission (PBC) in Security Council mandate design and mission transitions, lock in progress from the 2025 Peacebuilding Architecture Review, and promote predictable financing, inclusive governance, and the Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) agenda. We anticipate delicate negotiations with the Russian Federation and China regarding the scope of the PBC's engagement with the Council and references to broader structural drivers of conflict, which we balanced by explicitly reaffirming primary national ownership and the distinct mandates of UN principal organs. Ensuring consensus language on peacebuilding financing that respects the Fifth Committee and General Assembly prerogatives while acknowledging Council support will also require careful bridging.

messages.Algeria: Algeria appreciates Slovenia's initiative on this important draft resolution and supports its overall thrust. To ensure the resolution is comprehensive and effective, it is essential to adequately reflect the indispensable role of regional organizations—most notably the African Union and its PCRD framework—and to reaffirm that peacebuilding must strictly adhere to host-State consent, national sovereignty, and the structural root causes of conflict, particularly development. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder and Council colleagues to incorporate these priority elements.
messages.China: China appreciates Slovenia's initiative in preparing this draft resolution and supports strengthening the United Nations peacebuilding architecture on the basis of existing intergovernmental mandates. We emphasize that peacebuilding must strictly uphold national sovereignty and national ownership, ensuring that the Peacebuilding Commission operates with the consent of host countries. Furthermore, development is the foundation of lasting peace, and the draft should appropriately emphasize poverty eradication and economic development as central to addressing the root causes of conflict.
messages.Denmark: Denmark warmly welcomes and strongly supports Slovenia's initiative to table this ambitious and timely draft resolution ahead of the 2025 review of the peacebuilding architecture. As a steadfast supporter of the Peacebuilding Commission and a leading contributor to the Peacebuilding Fund, Denmark believes the text can be further enhanced by incorporating explicit language on human rights, civic space, the protection of women peacebuilders, and the intersection between climate risks and sustaining peace. We look forward to working closely and constructively with Slovenia and Council colleagues to bring this text to consensus.
messages.France: France warmly commends Slovenia for taking the initiative on this timely and well-balanced draft, which appropriately builds upon the Pact for the Future and strengthens the advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission. For France, sustaining peace and conflict prevention cannot be dissociated from the promotion and protection of human rights, which should be explicitly recognized alongside the rule of law and good governance in operative paragraph 5. We stand fully ready to engage constructively with all Council members to achieve a swift adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece warmly commends Slovenia for preparing a strong, balanced, and forward-looking draft resolution that rightly reinforces the peacebuilding architecture and reflects the commitments of the Pact for the Future. We fully support the emphasis on the advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission, predictable financing, and the indispensable participation of women and youth. Our proposed additions simply reinforce the foundational roles of international law, the peaceful settlement of disputes, and human rights in sustaining long-term peace.
messages.Guyana: Guyana welcomes Slovenia's initiative and broadly supports this balanced draft resolution, which strengthens the Council's engagement with the Peacebuilding Commission and reinforces the sustaining peace agenda. To ensure peacebuilding efforts remain comprehensive and forward-looking, we propose integrating explicit reference to addressing multidimensional root causes of conflict, particularly socioeconomic factors and the adverse impacts of climate change. We look forward to working constructively with all members towards the consensus adoption of this text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan welcomes Slovenia's timely initiative to strengthen the United Nations peacebuilding architecture, particularly in view of the 2025 review. As a major troop- and police-contributing country, we stress that effective peacebuilding and mission transitions require systematic consultations with T/PCCs and full respect for host-State consent and national ownership. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder to reflect these vital elements in the final text.
messages.Panama: Panama warmly welcomes and supports this timely draft resolution circulated by Slovenia ahead of the 2025 peacebuilding architecture review. We particularly appreciate the emphasis on the advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission, predictable financing, and the indispensable role of women and youth. We propose two minor additions to explicitly highlight the promotion of human rights and cooperation with regional and subregional organizations, which are essential to sustaining peace.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea commends Slovenia for taking the initiative to present this balanced and timely draft resolution ahead of the conclusion of the 2025 peacebuilding architecture review. As a committed advocate of sustaining peace and the Peacebuilding Commission, the Republic of Korea strongly supports making the PBC's advisory role more systematic and ensuring predictable financing. We believe the draft would be further enhanced by explicitly recognizing the critical role of partnerships with international financial institutions and regional organizations, as well as the fundamental contribution of the rule of law and human rights to sustaining peace.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation emphasizes that peacebuilding must strictly respect the principle of national ownership and host country consent, without infringing on the division of labour established by the UN Charter. We cannot accept any references to the Pact for the Future, from which our delegation formally disassociated. Furthermore, the advisory mandate of the Peacebuilding Commission must not be artificially expanded or imposed without the explicit consent of the concerned State.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone warmly welcomes Slovenia's initiative on this timely resolution ahead of the 2025 review of the peacebuilding architecture. As a country with direct experience of the transformative impact of United Nations peacebuilding and the Peacebuilding Commission, we attach great importance to national ownership, predictable financing, and strong partnerships. We urge the penholder to properly reflect the indispensable role of regional organizations, particularly the African Union, and to strengthen PBC collaboration with regional mechanisms.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes Slovenia's balanced draft and strongly supports strengthening the peacebuilding architecture, particularly during mission transitions and drawdowns. As a country undergoing vital security and political transitions, we emphasize that peacebuilding advice and mandate reviews must be conducted in close consultation with host States to safeguard national ownership. Furthermore, given the essential role of regional frameworks, we urge the inclusion of explicit language recognizing the strategic partnership between the United Nations, the Peacebuilding Commission, and regional organizations such as the African Union.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes Slovenia's timely and balanced draft, which appropriately reflects the outcomes of the Pact for the Future and the ongoing 2025 review of the peacebuilding architecture. To ensure a truly effective and durable approach to sustaining peace, we believe it is essential to explicitly highlight the foundational role of human rights, the rule of law, and an open civic space. We look forward to working constructively with all Council members towards an ambitious and consensual resolution.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks Slovenia for preparing this balanced and timely draft resolution ahead of the 2025 peacebuilding architecture review. We strongly support strengthening the advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission and advancing the Women, Peace, and Security and Youth, Peace, and Security agendas. Our proposed adjustments aim to preserve Council prerogatives on its working methods, underscore the indispensable role of human rights and civil society in sustaining peace, and appropriately reflect Member States' discussions on peacebuilding financing.

messages.Algeria: Algeria commends the penholder for its constructive engagement and welcomes the full incorporation of our priorities in Revision 1, notably the recognition of the African Union Post-Conflict Reconstruction and Development policy, predictable financing for African-led peacebuilding initiatives, and the robust affirmation of national sovereignty and ownership. We consider the revised draft well-balanced, addressing the root causes of conflict while respecting the primacy of host States, and we stand ready to support its adoption.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's constructive approach in accommodating our key proposals regarding national ownership, host State consultation, and the critical role of development and poverty eradication in peacebuilding. The current draft is well-balanced and reflects broad consensus across the Council. We propose a minor adjustment in operative paragraph 6 to rely on agreed Security Council terminology, which will facilitate unanimous adoption of the draft resolution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark expresses its sincere appreciation to Slovenia for skillfully steering this process and for incorporating our key priorities into Revision 1, notably on human rights, the protection of women peacebuilders and civil society, and climate-related security risks. The revised draft presents a balanced, comprehensive, and forward-looking text that strengthens the United Nations peacebuilding architecture ahead of the 2025 review. Denmark fully supports the draft resolution as currently formulated and stands ready to vote in favor.
messages.France: France thanks Slovenia for its constructive leadership as penholder and for incorporating our proposal regarding human rights into the draft resolution. The current text strikes an excellent balance, reflecting key priorities including the rule of law, the climate-security nexus, the Women and Peace and Security agenda, and predictable financing for peacebuilding. France is ready to support the adoption of this draft as currently formulated.
messages.Greece: Greece warmly thanks the penholder, Slovenia, for accommodating our proposals regarding the peaceful settlement of disputes and the promotion and protection of human rights. The revised draft represents a balanced, comprehensive, and forward-looking text that strengthens the United Nations peacebuilding architecture and enhances the advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission. Greece fully supports this draft resolution and stands ready to vote in favor.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for constructive engagement and for accommodating our priorities, particularly regarding the adverse impacts of climate change, socioeconomic disparities, and addressing root causes within peacebuilding strategies. The current draft strikes an appropriate balance across critical dimensions of sustaining peace and has Guyana's full support. We look forward to working towards its adoption.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan expresses its appreciation to the penholder for accommodating our priorities in revision 1, particularly by explicitly reflecting the vital role of troop- and police-contributing countries and the necessity of host State consent and national ownership. The revised draft strikes a well-calibrated balance that respects Charter principles, national sovereignty, and the imperative of addressing root causes through sustainable development. Pakistan is ready to support the adoption of this resolution.
messages.Panama: Panama commends Slovenia for its consultative leadership and expresses its full satisfaction with the revised text, which effectively accommodates our priorities on human rights, the rule of law, and partnerships with regional organizations. The draft provides a comprehensive and balanced framework that strengthens the UN peacebuilding architecture while addressing root causes and fostering inclusive participation of women, youth, and civil society. We look forward to voting in favor of this resolution.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks Slovenia for its constructive penholdership and for accommodating our proposals regarding partnerships with international financial institutions and the emphasis on human rights. The revised text strikes a sound, forward-looking balance that effectively reinforces the peacebuilding architecture, the advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission, and the sustaining peace agenda. We stand ready to support this resolution as drafted.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation reiterates its categorical objection to the inclusion of climate change language in Security Council products, as the Security Council is not the appropriate forum to address environmental phenomena. We also cannot accept non-consensual terminology such as 'human rights defenders' in OP6, nor artificial concepts like the 'triple nexus' in OP3 that blur the division of labour between principal UN organs. Should our fundamental red line regarding PP7 and our concerns on OP6 be accommodated, we stand ready to support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone commends the penholder for constructively incorporating our proposals into Revision 1, particularly regarding the strengthening of partnerships with the African Union and enhanced support for national post-conflict reconstruction capacities. The revised text strikes a balanced, comprehensive, and forward-looking approach to sustaining peace and the ongoing 2025 review of the peacebuilding architecture. Sierra Leone fully supports the draft resolution as presented and looks forward to its unanimous adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals into Revision 1, particularly on ensuring close consultation with host States and strengthening cooperation with regional organizations, especially the African Union. The revised draft effectively balances national ownership, predictable financing, and the vital role of regional partnerships in sustaining peace. Somalia fully supports this text and looks forward to its adoption.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks Slovenia for its constructive penholdership and warmly welcomes the incorporation of our proposals regarding human rights, civil society engagement, and the protection of women peacebuilders in revision 1. The draft presents a balanced, forward-looking text that strengthens the peacebuilding architecture and appropriately recognizes the vital roles of civil society, women, youth, and human rights in sustaining peace. We are ready to support the resolution as drafted.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks Slovenia for its constructive and transparent facilitation of this draft resolution. We appreciate the penholder's accommodation of our key priorities, particularly preserving Security Council prerogatives regarding the Peacebuilding Commission's advisory role, recognizing diverse perspectives on peacebuilding financing, and underscoring human rights and the essential participation of civil society. The current text strikes a balanced, forward-looking consensus, and the United States is pleased to support it.

before.Slovenia:
Mr. President,

Slovenia has the honour to present the draft resolution on peacebuilding and sustaining peace. 

Conflict prevention and sustaining peace are at the very core of Slovenia’s foreign policy and our engagement in the Security Council. In a global landscape marked by proliferating conflicts and severe challenges to the multilateral order, strengthening our collective peacebuilding architecture is not merely an option—it is an urgent necessity. 

This draft resolution builds upon the foundational work of resolutions 2282 and 2558, reaffirming our commitment to a holistic, coherent, and integrated approach across the United Nations system. It recognizes the vital, convening, and advisory role of the Peacebuilding Commission, particularly during critical transition phases, while underscoring that sustaining peace rests firmly upon national ownership, strong partnerships with regional organizations like the African Union, and the indispensable, full, equal, and meaningful participation of women and youth.

We extend our deep appreciation to all Council members for their constructive engagement throughout the negotiation process to reach a balanced, ambitious, and forward-looking text ahead of the 2025 review. We encourage all members of the Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution.

Thank you.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, and we commend the delegation of Slovenia for its constructive efforts throughout the negotiation process. 

Our vote reflects Algeria’s enduring conviction that lasting peace cannot be achieved solely through security responses. Peacebuilding requires a holistic approach that tackles the root causes of conflict, notably poverty, underdevelopment, institutional fragility, and social inequality. In this regard, the nexus between peace and development must remain at the heart of our collective action.

We welcome the resolution’s strong reaffirmation of the fundamental principles of national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence. Sustainable peace cannot be imposed from the outside; it must be nationally owned and nationally led, with the full consent of the host State and in strict alignment with national priorities and needs. The Peacebuilding Commission plays a valuable advisory role in this regard, and its engagement must always be guided by respect for national ownership.

Furthermore, we attach paramount importance to strengthening the strategic partnership between the United Nations and regional organizations, particularly the African Union, in accordance with Chapter VIII of the Charter. As our continent bears a significant share of peacebuilding challenges, the implementation of the African Union Post-Conflict Reconstruction and Development policy and the provision of predictable, adequate, and sustainable financing for African-led initiatives are essential. 

As we engage in the 2025 review of the United Nations peacebuilding architecture, Algeria remains committed to working constructively with all partners to ensure a more coherent, responsive, and effective system that delivers tangible results on the ground.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We thank the delegation of Slovenia for its constructive efforts throughout the consultation process.

Peacebuilding is a vital pillar of the work of the United Nations. Amidst complex and intertwined global security challenges, supporting countries emerging from conflict in achieving durable peace and sustainable development is more critical than ever. In this context, China wishes to emphasize the following points:

First, national ownership must always remain the core principle of peacebuilding. The primary responsibility for sustaining peace lies with national governments. The United Nations and the international community must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of the countries concerned, adhere strictly to the principle of host-country consent, and tailor support to national development priorities rather than imposing external models or conditionalities.

Second, development is the foundation for sustaining peace. Security and development are mutually reinforcing. To effectively prevent conflict and avoid relapses, international efforts must prioritize addressing root causes, notably through poverty eradication, economic recovery, infrastructure development, and capacity-building. We hope the United Nations peacebuilding architecture will continue to enhance synergy with international financial institutions and development agencies to deliver tangible development benefits to host nations.

Third, the division of labour among United Nations organs must be respected. As an advisory body bridging the Security Council, the General Assembly, and the Economic and Social Council, the Peacebuilding Commission should perform its duties strictly within its mandate, providing timely, objective, and actionable advice to the Security Council upon request, without infringing upon the Council’s primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security.

Finally, peacebuilding financing must be adequate, predictable, and managed with transparency and accountability. We encourage traditional donors to fulfill their commitments and scale up voluntary contributions, while supporting regional and subregional organizations, in particular the African Union, in their post-conflict reconstruction and peacebuilding endeavors.

China actively supports the 2025 review of the United Nations peacebuilding architecture. Together with the international community, through initiatives such as the Global Security Initiative and the Global Development Initiative, China stands ready to continue contributing constructively to sustaining peace and realizing common security worldwide.

Thank you, Mr. President.

As we engage in the 2025 review of the United Nations peacebuilding architecture, today’s unanimous adoption sends a clear signal of our shared commitment. after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation supported the resolution submitted by Slovenia on peacebuilding and sustaining peace. 

Our delegation has consistently advocated for enhancing the effectiveness of the United Nations peacebuilding architecture, whose central pillar remains the Peacebuilding Commission. We appreciate the efforts of the penholder to accommodate the views of delegations during the negotiations, which allowed the Council to reach consensus.

At the same time, we deem it necessary to state our principled position on several key aspects.

First and foremost, the primary responsibility for peacebuilding and sustaining peace rests with national Governments. International assistance in post-conflict recovery and peacebuilding must strictly respect national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence. It can only be provided upon the request and with the full consent of the host State, taking into account its specific national priorities, historical context, and local realities. Imposing external recipes or intrusive political conditions is counterproductive and undermines sustainable recovery.

Second, in strengthening cooperation between the Security Council and the Peacebuilding Commission, it is essential to strictly adhere to the division of labour established by the Charter of the United Nations. The advisory nature of the PBC must be fully respected. The Commission should not duplicate the functions of the Council, nor should it infringe upon the Council’s primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. Seeking the advice of the PBC, particularly during transitions and mandate reviews, must be done on a case-by-case basis and only with the explicit agreement of the host country concerned.

Third, regarding peacebuilding financing, we underline that voluntary contributions must remain the primary source of funding for the Peacebuilding Fund. Decisions concerning UN financing, including any assessed contributions, fall strictly within the competence of the General Assembly and its Fifth Committee. 

Finally, peacebuilding efforts should focus on genuine, practical assistance to post-conflict countries—primarily on the restoration of state institutions, basic infrastructure, socioeconomic development, and poverty eradication. Attempts to artificially overburden the peacebuilding agenda with politically sensitive concepts or to shift its focus away from these fundamental tasks risk undermining the core mission of the peacebuilding architecture.

We trust that these considerations will be duly taken into account as the 2025 review of the peacebuilding architecture continues.

Thank you.
